tagline: Extending and testing the Kiraly and Tokai dictionary of the Rohonc Codex
intro:
The Rohonc Codex is a small paper book from the sixteenth century. It contains about 450 leaves and is kept at the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in Budapest. It is written in a unique script that runs from right to left and uses several hundred signs, with mostly one sign per word or phrase.

Levente Zoltan Kiraly and Gabor Tokai established what the book contains. They identified the apocryphal Life of Adam and Eve running into the legend of the Rood, the story of Joachim and Anne, a Passion the codex itself says it takes from Matthew and John, sermons and parables for the gospels of the year, the Finding of the Cross, the Acts of the Apostles, and at the end a few pages of one man's diary. The frame is a revelation where an angel of God speaks and the prophet Elijah is the one addressed.

This project started from the dictionary of Kiraly and Tokai. It tested and extended their work by reading signs their dictionary leaves undefined, checking every reading at every place the sign stands in the book, and rendering the whole manuscript into English with every word marked by how well it is known.
how_far: The project read most of the manuscript. The figures below show how far the reading goes.
tiers: The dictionary of added readings is sorted into tiers. Tier A readings survive every place the sign stands in the book, or are proved by an identical formula or a numeral. Tier B readings survive most places, with the rest unclear rather than against. Tiers C and D are read from one passage with nothing inside the book able to refuse them. Tier G is a guess, printed in brackets, and counted as read nowhere. Withdrawn readings stay in the file with the reason they went.

is_it_true: The readings were tested. Every test bar was declared before it ran and none was moved. Failures are recorded beside passes. The summary is below.

edition: The whole manuscript is being set as a book in two parts. It will contain a continuous retelling by episode and all 441 folios with their marked lines. It is being finished and will appear in the OONA Free Library. Nothing on this site waits on it.
credit: The manuscript is out of copyright. Kiraly and Tokai's dictionary, transcription and page images are theirs. They are credited on every page and linked, not rehosted. The readings, tests, English and editorial matter are this project's own. Every figure on the site is read out of a saved run, never typed by hand.
reading_lead: This page gives one paragraph of English for each of the 441 folios, in Kiraly and Tokai's page order. Restorations are in brackets. The full per-word marks are in the edition and the rendering, not on this page.
dictionary_lead:
This dictionary contains the readings this project added. It does not reproduce the 841 entries of Kiraly and Tokai. The signs are written as glyph codes, using three hexadecimal digits per glyph. The drawn signs are on the site of Kiraly and Tokai.

The dictionary is searchable by reading or sign and can be filtered by tier. Each entry shows the evidence line. It includes tier A, B, C, D, and G readings, and withdrawn readings.
data_lead: This page provides every file the site pages are built from. The files include the dictionary and folio English as JSON, the rendering, the reader's edition, every saved run, and the outside readers' replies.
outside_lead: Two outside reviewers were shown the write-up and asked what tests they would require. Those tests were run as they specified. One reviewer's full specification is quoted here.
credit_line: This project rests on the dictionary of Kiraly and Tokai; their translation is unpublished, and the readings here are this project's own.
